questions.question: The Government _____ is a statement of expected receipts and expected expenditures of the Government (for the coming fiscal year) that reveals the budgetary policy of the Government to achieve the twin objective of growth and stability.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A government budget is an annual financial statement that outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year.
 
• In India, it is a constitutional requirement (Article 112) that the government give a statement of estimated income and expenditures to Parliament for each financial year that runs from April 1 to March 31.
 
• This 'Annual Financial Statement' is the government's primary budget document.
 
• Budgets are grouped into three categories based on these estimates:
 
 
• Balanced budget.
 
• Surplus budget.
 
• Deficit budget.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A government budget is said to be a balanced budget if the estimated government expenditures in a given fiscal year are equal to the expected government receipts.

 
 
• A balanced budget ensures economic stability if implemented successfully.
 
• A balanced budget is Inapplicable in less developed countries as it limits the scope of economic growth.
 
 
 
• A government budget is said to be a surplus budget if the expected government revenues exceed the estimated government expenditure in a particular financial year.
 
 
• A country's financial wealth is indicated by a surplus budget.
 
 
 
• If the estimated government expenditure exceeds the expected government revenue in a given fiscal year, the budget is considered to be a deficit budget.
 
 
• A deficit budget is best suited for developing economies, such as India

questions.question: The first five year plan of India was based on ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harrod-Domar Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First Five Year Plan:**__

 __
 
• The first Indian prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, presented the First Five-Year Plan to the Parliament of India.
 
• The First Five-year Plan was launched in 1951 which mainly focused on the development of the primary sector.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on the **Harrod–Domar model with few modifications.**
 
• The target growth rate was 2.1% annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth; the achieved growth rate was 3.6% the net domestic product went up by 15.
 
• Many irrigation projects were initiated during this period, including the Bhakra, Hirakud, Mettur Dam, and Damodar Valley dams.
 
• At the end of the plan period in 1956, five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were started and The University Grants Commission (UGC) was set up.
 
• Contracts were signed to start five steel plants, which existed in the middle of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• The plan was quasi-successful for the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basic information about **planning commission and 5-year plans:**

 
 
• Planning commission** founded: 1950.**
 
• Planning Commission** head**:** Prime Minister**
 
• **First five-year plan **launched: in **1951**
 
• A** total** number of **5-year plans**: **12.**
 
• **Last **five-year plan: **2012 to 2017** (Under PM Manmohan Singh).
 
• Planning Commission** dissolved**: **2014** (By** PM Narendra Modi**).

• Kathak dance originated from Uttar Pradesh (U.P) in North India.
 
• It was primarily a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures.
 
• Usually a solo performance, the dancer often pauses to recite verses followed by their execution through movement.
 
• Kathak is the only form of classical dance that belongs to North Indian music.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, the Right to protection of life and personal liberty is a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Right of an Individual**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to Article 21: “Protection of Life and Personal Liberty: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.”
 
• This fundamental right is available to every person, citizens and foreigners alike.
 
• Article 21 provides two rights:
 
 
• Right to life
 
• Right to personal liberty
 
 
 
• The fundamental right provided by Article 21 is one of the most important rights that the Constitution guarantees.
 
• The Supreme Court of India has described this right as the ‘heart of fundamental rights’. 
 
• The right specifically mentions that no person shall be deprived of life and liberty except as per the procedure established by law. This implies that this right has been provided against the State only. State here includes not just the government, but also, government departments, local bodies, the Legislatures, etc.

questions.question: As of October 2023, who among the following is the governor of Odisha?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Raghubar Das has previously served as the Chief Minister of Jharkhand.
 
• He is known for his administrative skills and contributions to regional development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor of a State**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor's role is largely ceremonial, but they have the power to summon, prorogue, or dissolve the state legislature.
 
• They also play a crucial role in the appointment of the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Raghubar Das**
 
 
• Raghubar Das is an Indian politician and a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• He served as the 6th Chief Minister of Jharkhand from December 2014 to December 2019.
 
• He has been actively involved in politics for several decades and has held various significant positions within the party and government.
 
• His tenure as Chief Minister was marked by various developmental projects and reforms.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**
 
 
• Odisha is a state located in the eastern part of India.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage, historical monuments, and natural beauty.
 
• Bhubaneswar is the capital city of Odisha, which is also known as the 'Temple City of India'.
 
• The state has a diverse economy with agriculture, mining, and tourism being the major sectors.

questions.question: According to the 2011 census of India, the literacy rate in India is ____ percent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**74.04**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The literacy rate in India as per the 2011 census is **74.04%**.
 
• The literacy rate is an important indicator of a country's educational development and human resource quality.
 
• The census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The 2011 census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who are able to read and write with understanding, among the population aged 7 years and above.
 
• A higher literacy rate indicates better educational opportunities and improved socio-economic conditions.
 
• In 2001, the literacy rate in India was 64.8%, showing a significant improvement in 2011.
 
• Factors affecting literacy rates include access to education, quality of education, government policies, socio-economic conditions, and cultural attitudes towards education.
 
 
 
• **Census**
 
 
• The Census of India is one of the largest administrative exercises in the world, aiming to capture detailed information about the population.
 
• The first synchronous census in India was held in 1881, and it has been conducted every decade since then.
 
• The census collects data on various parameters such as population size, demographics, economic activity, literacy, housing, and amenities.
 
• Data from the census is crucial for planning, policy-making, and administration at various levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy**
 
 
• Literacy is a key component of human development, enabling individuals to access information, improve their socio-economic status, and participate fully in society.
 
• It has a direct impact on health, employment, and income levels, contributing to overall national development.
 
• Efforts to improve literacy rates include government initiatives such as the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and National Literacy Mission.
 
• Non-governmental organizations and community-based programs also play a significant role in promoting literacy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a 's' block element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rubidium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rubidium (Rb)** is an element that belongs to the s-block of the periodic table.
 
• It is an alkali metal and is found in Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• Rubidium has an atomic number of 37 and is characterized by having a single electron in its outermost s-orbital.
 
• Alkali metals, including Rubidium, are known for their high reactivity and are typically stored under oil to prevent reaction with air or water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **s-block Elements**

 
 
• The s-block elements are those in which the outermost electrons occupy an s-orbital. These elements are found in Groups 1 and 2 of the periodic table.
 
• Group 1 elements are known as alkali metals and include Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Cesium (Cs), and Francium (Fr).
 
• Group 2 elements are known as alkaline earth metals and include Beryllium (Be), Magnesium (Mg), Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba), and Radium (Ra).
 
• These elements are characterized by their high reactivity, especially with water, and they form basic (alkaline) solutions when they react with water.
 
 
 
• **d-block Elements**
 
 
• The d-block elements are those in which the outermost electrons occupy a d-orbital. These elements are found in Groups 3 to 12 of the periodic table.
 
• They are often referred to as transition metals and include elements like Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), and Gold (Au).
 
• Transition metals are characterized by their ability to form variable oxidation states and colored compounds.
 
• They are also known for their catalytic properties and high conductivity of electricity and heat.

questions.question: Average density of population in India is ____ persons per square km, according to 2011 census of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons per square km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, the average density of population in India is **382 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of people per unit area, typically per square kilometer.
 
• The density of population is an important metric for understanding how crowded or spacious a region is.
 
• States like Bihar and West Bengal have higher densities compared to states like Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density**

 
 
• Population density is a measurement of the number of people living per unit of area (e.g., per square kilometer).
 
• It is a crucial statistic for urban planning, resource allocation, and understanding demographic trends.
 
• High population density areas may face challenges like overcrowding, strain on infrastructure, and resource depletion.
 
• Conversely, low population density areas might struggle with economic development and access to services.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census of India**
 
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the 15th National census since 1871.
 
• It collected comprehensive data on population, economic activity, literacy and education, housing and household amenities, urbanization, fertility, and mortality.
 
• The total population of India as per the 2011 Census was approximately 1.21 billion.
 
• The data from the census is crucial for policy formulation, planning, and administration at various levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations in Population Density**
 
 
• India exhibits significant regional variations in population density.
 
• Northern states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have very high population densities.
 
• Eastern states like West Bengal also exhibit high density, while northeastern states like Arunachal Pradesh have very low density.
 
• These variations are due to factors like geography, climate, availability of resources, and historical settlement patterns.
 
 
 
• **Implications of Population Density**
 
 
• High population density can lead to issues such as overcrowding, pollution, and strain on infrastructure and resources.
 
• Low population density can result in challenges related to economic development, social isolation, and inefficient service delivery.
 
• Understanding population density helps in urban planning, disaster management, and infrastructure development.
 
• Policies aimed at balanced regional development often consider population density metrics.

questions.question: Who among the following won the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup 2023, marking a historic achievement.
 
• The tournament was held in South Africa, and the final match took place on 29 January 2023.
 
• India defeated England by 7 wickets in the final to clinch the title.
 
• This victory is significant as it showcases the growing talent and potential of women's cricket in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup**

 
 
• The ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup is an international cricket tournament organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for national teams with players under the age of 19.
 
• It is the inaugural edition of the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup, aimed at providing young women cricketers with a platform to showcase their talent on a global stage.
 
• The tournament format includes a round-robin stage followed by knockout rounds, including semi-finals and the final.
 
• Participating teams from various cricketing nations compete in this tournament, promoting the development of women's cricket worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Women's Cricket in India**
 
 
• Women's cricket in India has seen significant growth over the past few years, with increased participation and performance on the international stage.
 
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has been instrumental in promoting women's cricket through domestic tournaments like the Women's T20 Challenge.
 
• Indian women's cricket team has achieved notable success, including reaching the finals of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup and ICC Women's Cricket World Cup.
 
• The victory in the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup 2023 is expected to further inspire young girls to take up the sport and pursue a career in cricket.
 
 
 
• **International Cricket Council (ICC)**
 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for the organization and governance of major international cricket tournaments.
 
• Founded in 1909, the ICC's headquarters are located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
 
• The ICC organizes events like the ICC Cricket World Cup, ICC T20 World Cup, ICC Champions Trophy, and ICC U19 Cricket World Cup.
 
• The ICC's mission is to promote and develop the game of cricket worldwide, ensuring fair play and integrity in the sport.

questions.question: ____ was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahadev Govind Ranade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade was a distinguished Indian scholar, social reformer, and author.
 
• He co-founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861, which advocated for the rights and remarriage of widows.
 
• Ranade was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress and played a significant role in India's social and political movements.
 
• He was also a judge of the Bombay High Court and a staunch supporter of social reforms such as the abolition of child marriage and the promotion of women's education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen**

 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen was an influential Indian social reformer who was associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He worked towards the abolition of sati, child marriage, and the promotion of women's education.
 
• He established the Indian Reform Association in 1870, which aimed at promoting social and educational reforms.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang**
 
 
• Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang was a notable Indian physician and social reformer.
 
• He was one of the founders of the Prarthana Samaj, which aimed at reforming social customs and religious practices in India.
 
• He worked towards the upliftment of women and the eradication of caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Debendra Nath Tagore**
 
 
• Debendra Nath Tagore was an eminent Indian philosopher and religious reformer, associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore, the famous poet and Nobel laureate.
 
• He played a crucial role in the Brahmo Samaj movement, which aimed at reforming Hindu society and religion.
